content.comment_body: Hello, My setup involves four 4-20 mA sensors in the building corners. I would like to display these readings wirelessly in the control room, seeking an affordable solution. The initial idea is to use [product_name] modules at each sensor location and one master [product_name] in the control room. While radio communication is ideal, I haven’t found a suitable TCP/IP-to-radio device from [company_name]. Has anyone tried something similar? Any suggestions for a budget-friendly solution?

[product_name] modules do not support wireless communication directly. You’ll need a WLAN device with LAN outputs, for example, Scalance W720/760. Are you certain [product_name] modules can interface with your sensors? What communication protocol do the sensors use?

Scalance W devices are quite costly. The sensors operate on 4-20 mA, so they’re compatible with [product_name]. Here’s a link to a more affordable wireless PLC module: [url]. I’m looking for similar, inexpensive radio communication solutions.
How do you plan to transmit a 4-20 mA signal over WLAN?

Essentially, [product_name] modules can read the 4-20 mA sensor as a slave and send the data via TCP/IP. Another [product_name] module would act as the master and receive the signals via TCP/IP. I think the wireless medium shouldn’t pose significant issues.

If you have a router, you only need access points or WLAN repeaters with LAN connectors. Most routers can connect with WLAN repeaters, allowing all devices plugged into the repeater’s LAN port to be accessed via the router where your master [product_name] is located. Start with a single repeater and expand as needed, but check the maximum number of repeaters your router supports.
To network [product_name] modules within the same environment, I use IOGEAR Ethernet-2-WiFi Universal Wireless Adapters, which are available on Amazon for about $45. Here is the link: [url]
You could also consider the TP-Link Nano router. It’s configurable as a WLAN router or repeater, includes a LAN connector, is compact, and is reasonably priced. Hope this information is useful.

analysis.insight_summary: Users intend to create a wireless 4-20mA sensor monitoring setup using [product_name] modules, focusing on affordability. The lack of an accessible wireless TCP/IP radio device from [company_name], and the high cost of branded alternatives, drives users to explore third-party WLAN repeaters and wireless adapters. The main challenge is obtaining economical, integrated wireless options for small-scale installations that involve [product_name].
analysis.user_expectations: Users are seeking a simple, budget-friendly way to wirelessly connect multiple [product_name] modules to transfer sensor data via TCP/IP, ideally with devices from [company_name].
